The test image shows a soybean plant pulled from the ground with the stem visible. The stem appears to have whitish/light-colored tissue, and the plant looks wilted. I can see what appears to be fluffy white growth on the stem area. This is a stem/whole plant symptom.

Top candidates from stem classes: White_Mold, Phytophthora, Charcoal_Rot, Rhizoctonia, Fusarium, Anthracnose, Green_stem_disorder, Brown_Stem_Rot.

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with different candidates.
White Mold reference shows bleached stems with dark sclerotia. The test image has a different appearance. Let me check Phytophthora.
This White Mold reference shows dark sclerotia and white cottony growth on stems with green pods. Let me check Fusarium and Phytophthora whole plant views.

I've now used all 8 reference image views across 8 different classes (White_Mold x2, Phytophthora x2, Charcoal_Rot, Rhizoctonia, Pythium_damping_off, Fusarium).

**Analysis of test image:**
- Soybean plant pulled from the ground and laid on grass
- Stem appears bleached/whitish with what looks like fluffy white cottony growth along portions
- Wilting green leaves still attached
- Plant appears collapsed/dead

**Key differentiators:**
- The white fluffy/cottony growth on the stem is the hallmark sign of White Mold (Sclerotinia)
- Charcoal Rot shows dark microsclerotia specks, not white fluffy growth
- Phytophthora shows dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration, not white
- Rhizoctonia shows reddish-brown dry cankers at soil line on seedlings
- Fusarium shows internal brown vascular tissue without external white growth
- The bleached, soft stem appearance with cottony white mycelium matches White Mold descriptions: "infected stems become soft, watery, and bleached white" with "fluffy white mold growth"
